criteria.semantics: A native <figure> holding an element of role img named by the visual's label (aria-label), and a <figcaption> with its description in words: what the picture shows is there as text.

keyboard.outcome: Passes it by: it is not a stop in the tab order.

criteria.name: The visual's label.
criteria.group: The description, in the figure's caption.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the caption grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the visual scale down and its caption wrap, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <figure> element.
The picture is one element of role img.
The picture is named by the visual's label in aria-label.
I SEE the description in a <figcaption> under the picture.
A visual is not a control: nothing in it is a stop in the tab order.
WHEN I reach the visual with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR its label and the role of image, then its caption.
WHEN I swipe to it with a mobile screen reader (TalkBack, VoiceOver) I HEAR its label and its caption.

criteria.semantics: The window draws no picture: a visual falls back to text, its label and description in fg on bg. Once GPUI draws it and exposes a tree: an AccessKit Image named by its label, described by its description.

keyboard.outcome: Pass the visual by: it is no stop of its own; the controls before and after it are.

criteria.name: The visual's label.

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the label and description grow with it, with no loss of information.

WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the label and description drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the label and description at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the label and description drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) I SEE the label and description whole and legible in the magnified view.

check.statement: I SEE the visual's label and description as text in its place.
WHEN I reach the visual's place with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR its label and its description.

announce.api: AXImage, its label as the AXDescription and its description as the AXHelp (AccessKit Role::Image).
announce.says: "Sales by month, image", then its description.

announce.api: ControlType Image, its label as the Name and its description as the FullDescription.
ATSPI_ROLE_IMAGE, its label as the name and its description as the description.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size and the platform's high contrast, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs, every_gpui_see_check_with_a_probe_holds), which no CI job runs yet; the rest are reported as not verified.
